name: Fast Transformer Decoding: One Write-Head is All You Need
problem: Autoregressive decoding of a transformer is memory-bandwidth-bound, not compute-bound, because every step re-reads the large key and value tensors from HBM - and those tensors grow with the number of attention heads.
mechanism: Multi-query attention: share ONE key head and ONE value head across all query heads, so the per-step KV read shrinks by the number of attention heads. Training is unchanged in cost (the attention computation is unchanged in shape); only the decode-time memory traffic drops. Squeezes the KV cache from H heads to 1.
speedup_reported: QUALITATIVE ONLY, and the paper is careful about this: 'we verify experimentally that the resulting models can indeed be MUCH FASTER to decode, and incur only minor quality degradation from the baseline'. No multiple, no baseline engine, no hardware. The mechanism argument is the durable claim: decode is bandwidth-bound, so shrinking the KV tensor by the head count is a direct bandwidth reduction. Any specific decode-tok/s figure attributed to this paper would be borrowed from a later implementation.
